chunk_findings.detail: The added validator references `SECURITY_DISCLOSE` on the line `if "disclose" in t and t["disclose"] not in SECURITY_DISCLOSE:` and in the error message, but this diff adds only `SECURITY_TABLE_KEYS` and no import of `SECURITY_DISCLOSE`. Therefore loading any `[export.security]` table (for example `disclose = "ids"`) makes `_export_table_problem` call `_security_keys_problem` and raise `NameError` instead of returning a validation message, so the security export config cannot be validated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/export.py:_security_keys_problem

chunk_findings.detail: `collect` only returns `versions`, `open`, and `fixed`. It never queries security-pass findings or dependency-advisory data, so a recorded security finding, or an unfixed dependency advisory with no matching `Bug`, is absent from the generated SECURITY.md Known Issues and vulnerable-version marks. The intended change requires known issues from open/fixed security-tagged bugs and the security pass, and vulnerable versions for unfixed dependency advisories; this data function makes that impossible for the SECURITY doc type that reuses it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:collect

chunk_findings.detail: `_versions` identifies the current release line by absolute newest git tag: the first row inserted gets `newest=True` because of `not rows`. If an old maintenance line receives a backport tag after the newer major release (for example `1.5.9` tagged after `2.0.0`) and `1.5` is not in `cfg.flow.lines`, `_status` still returns `"supported"` for `1.5`. SECURITY.md then marks an EOL/old line as supported even though only the current release line should be supported by default.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_versions

chunk_findings.detail: The new `target_of` probes the filesystem directly with `(Path(repo) / rel).is_file()` instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, violating [r-adapters] (“filesystem layout” must use an adapter so tests and swaps touch one place). A concrete failure: if an `also_at` directory such as `repo/.github` exists but is unreadable, `Path.is_file()` can raise `PermissionError` and crash refresh/status even when the actual target `spec.path` exists and would have been used directly; an adapter-backed filesystem check would keep that behavior isolated and testable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:target_of

chunk_findings.detail: When an existing CRLF file lacks a region and `force` is true, `_appended` builds each region with `render_region(doc, n, bodies[n])`; that embeds the `body-sha256` of the LF body from `rendered`, and only afterwards converts LF to CRLF in the whole block with `.replace("\n", eol)`. The appended region's body bytes in the file are then CRLF while its `body-sha256` marker hashes the LF body. Example: a CRLF `SECURITY.md` without the managed block, when exported with `--force`, gets a block whose body hash does not match its body. The next non-force refresh sees that mismatch as a hand-edited region and refuses to update it (or reports drift), so the file does not stabilize after the operator confirms the append.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/regions.py:_appended

chunk_findings.detail: The known-issues section ends with “Dependency advisories and security-pass findings are not recorded there, so they are not covered here.” This contradicts the stated intent that the known issues must include “findings of the security pass,” and the requirement that a version carrying an unfixed dependency advisory be marked vulnerable. Given a security-pass finding, the generated SECURITY.md will either omit it while falsely claiming it is not covered, or list it while the text says it is not, making the exported security policy inaccurate. The same omission is echoed in ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md, which says known issues come only from bugs tagged `security` or `secbug`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2

chunk_findings.detail: The test helper `git()` invokes `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], ...)`, a direct external subprocess tool. This violates [r-adapters], which requires every external dependency (including git and subprocess tools) to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. The new test file therefore introduces an out-of-adapter dependency in the change.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_security.py:git

chunk_findings.detail: In `ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2`, the `known-issues` region wraps both the `open` and `fixed` loops inside an `{% if open or fixed %}` check, but the closing `{% endcall %}` is placed *after* the explanatory text ("These are the bugs recorded as security issues..."). When both `open` and `fixed` are empty, the template falls through to `{% else %}` and renders "None recorded." inside the region, but because the explanation follows the `{% if %}` block and is outside it, an empty project will render the "None recorded." line *followed by* the explanatory text saying "These are the bugs recorded as security issues in this project's log...", which is contradictory and misleading since no bugs are recorded at all.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2:23

chunk_findings.detail: The function references `SECURITY_DISCLOSE` (`if "disclose" in t and t["disclose"] not in SECURITY_DISCLOSE:`), but this symbol is not defined or imported anywhere in this change to `ddflow/config_sections/export.py`. With a config containing `[export.security] disclose = "ids"` (or any disclose value), `_export_table_problem("security", {"disclose": "ids"})` reaches that line and raises `NameError: name 'SECURITY_DISCLOSE' is not defined` instead of returning a validation error, so security export config validation crashes for the new knob.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/export.py:_security_keys_problem

chunk_findings.detail: `collect()` passes every security-tagged non-invalid bug to `_vulnerable()`, but `_vulnerable()` treats any bug without a `_Fix` as unfixed. A bug resolved `duplicate` (or `wontfix`, `notabug`) is not in `fixes` and `b.open` is false, so it is intentionally absent from the open/fixed known-issue lists, yet `_vulnerable()` still emits `vulnerable: <id>, not fixed yet` for the newest release. Concrete input: SEC-10 is tagged `security`, closed as duplicate of fixed bug SEC-0, and has no fix task. The SECURITY.md will permanently mark all current releases vulnerable to SEC-10, even though SEC-10 is a closed duplicate and SEC-0 is fixed. `_vulnerable()` should ignore non-open bugs that are not in `fixes`, matching the known-issues scope of open and fixed bugs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_vulnerable

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper queries the filesystem directly with `os.path.isfile(Path(repo) / rel)` instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, contrary to [r-adapters]. This is a new external dependency in `ddflow/services/export/ops.py`—e.g. every `target_of(repo, spec)` call performs ad-hoc filesystem-layout access that cannot be swapped or faked through the adapter layer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:target_of

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper’s docstring promises “a blank line before each” appended missing region, but it builds `block` with `"\n".join(render_region(...) for n in names)`, which inserts only a single newline between consecutive region blocks. Since `render_region` returns a region ending at the end marker without a trailing newline (a newline after `-->` would be outside the region), using `force` to append more than one missing region produces adjacent end/start markers with no blank line, e.g. `<!-- ...:supported:end -->\n<!-- ...:known:start -->`. The exported SECURITY.md therefore loses the blank-line separation present in the template and can render its supported/known-issue sections incorrectly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/regions.py: _appended

chunk_findings.detail: The template says "Dependency advisories and security-pass findings are not recorded there, so they are not covered here," and the matching help text in ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md describes Known Issues as only "bugs tagged `security` or `secbug`." This contradicts the change's own intent: dependency advisories are required to be shown in the Supported Versions table as "vulnerable: <id>, fixed in <ver>", and Known Issues must include "findings of the security pass." Given a dependency advisory or a security-pass finding, the exported SECURITY.md tells readers the item is not covered (or is omitted if the backend follows this text), so the required security disclosure is missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2:48-49

chunk_findings.detail: This new test file violates [r-adapters]: the helper `git()` calls `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], ...)` directly, and later tests also manipulate the filesystem with `Path`/`os` instead of using the project’s adapter ports. The rule explicitly lists `git`, `subprocess tools`, and `filesystem layout` as external dependencies that must go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, with tests using fakes rather than real subprocesses. Any environment without `git` on `PATH` makes every fixture in this file fail with `FileNotFoundError`, and the tests are not isolated behind a swappable fake as required.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_security.py:git

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation of `_is_security` checks `bool(wanted & set(b.tags)) or (item is not None and bool(wanted & set(item.tags)))`. However, `b.tags` and `item.tags` are expected to be collections of strings, but if either `b.tags` or `item.tags` is `None` or not an iterable of strings (for instance, if `Item.tags` can be `None` or another type based on the core model), `set(b.tags)` or `set(item.tags)` will raise a `TypeError` when `collect(q)` is executed. Given the core model fields for bugs and items, `tags` might be `None`, leading to a crash on export execution.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: The function references `SECURITY_DISCLOSE` (`if "disclose" in t and t["disclose"] not in SECURITY_DISCLOSE:`), but this symbol is not defined or imported anywhere in this change to `ddflow/config_sections/export.py`. With a config containing `[export.security] disclose = "ids"` (or any disclose value), `_export_table_problem("security", {"disclose": "ids"})` reaches that line and raises `NameError: name 'SECURITY_DISCLOSE' is not defined` instead of returning a validation error, so security export config validation crashes for the new knob.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/export.py:_security_keys_problem

chunk_findings.detail: `collect()` passes every security-tagged non-invalid bug to `_vulnerable()`, but `_vulnerable()` treats any bug without a `_Fix` as unfixed. A bug resolved `duplicate` (or `wontfix`, `notabug`) is not in `fixes` and `b.open` is false, so it is intentionally absent from the open/fixed known-issue lists, yet `_vulnerable()` still emits `vulnerable: <id>, not fixed yet` for the newest release. Concrete input: SEC-10 is tagged `security`, closed as duplicate of fixed bug SEC-0, and has no fix task. The SECURITY.md will permanently mark all current releases vulnerable to SEC-10, even though SEC-10 is a closed duplicate and SEC-0 is fixed. `_vulnerable()` should ignore non-open bugs that are not in `fixes`, matching the known-issues scope of open and fixed bugs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_vulnerable

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper queries the filesystem directly with `os.path.isfile(Path(repo) / rel)` instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, contrary to [r-adapters]. This is a new external dependency in `ddflow/services/export/ops.py`—e.g. every `target_of(repo, spec)` call performs ad-hoc filesystem-layout access that cannot be swapped or faked through the adapter layer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:target_of

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper’s docstring promises “a blank line before each” appended missing region, but it builds `block` with `"\n".join(render_region(...) for n in names)`, which inserts only a single newline between consecutive region blocks. Since `render_region` returns a region ending at the end marker without a trailing newline (a newline after `-->` would be outside the region), using `force` to append more than one missing region produces adjacent end/start markers with no blank line, e.g. `<!-- ...:supported:end -->\n<!-- ...:known:start -->`. The exported SECURITY.md therefore loses the blank-line separation present in the template and can render its supported/known-issue sections incorrectly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/regions.py: _appended

chunk_findings.detail: The template says "Dependency advisories and security-pass findings are not recorded there, so they are not covered here," and the matching help text in ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md describes Known Issues as only "bugs tagged `security` or `secbug`." This contradicts the change's own intent: dependency advisories are required to be shown in the Supported Versions table as "vulnerable: <id>, fixed in <ver>", and Known Issues must include "findings of the security pass." Given a dependency advisory or a security-pass finding, the exported SECURITY.md tells readers the item is not covered (or is omitted if the backend follows this text), so the required security disclosure is missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2:48-49

chunk_findings.detail: This new test file violates [r-adapters]: the helper `git()` calls `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], ...)` directly, and later tests also manipulate the filesystem with `Path`/`os` instead of using the project’s adapter ports. The rule explicitly lists `git`, `subprocess tools`, and `filesystem layout` as external dependencies that must go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, with tests using fakes rather than real subprocesses. Any environment without `git` on `PATH` makes every fixture in this file fail with `FileNotFoundError`, and the tests are not isolated behind a swappable fake as required.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_security.py:git

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation of `_is_security` checks `bool(wanted & set(b.tags)) or (item is not None and bool(wanted & set(item.tags)))`. However, `b.tags` and `item.tags` are expected to be collections of strings, but if either `b.tags` or `item.tags` is `None` or not an iterable of strings (for instance, if `Item.tags` can be `None` or another type based on the core model), `set(b.tags)` or `set(item.tags)` will raise a `TypeError` when `collect(q)` is executed. Given the core model fields for bugs and items, `tags` might be `None`, leading to a crash on export execution.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: The new `none_here = len(sp.missing) == len(bodies)` is also true when `bodies` is empty — i.e. a bare-document export with no managed regions, a case the function already supports via its `bare_doc` parameter. For an existing bare-document target, `sp.missing` is empty, so `len(sp.missing) == len(bodies)` is `0 == 0`; without `--force` this sets `refuse` (“... has no ddflow region ...”) and `W._finish` refuses the write even though nothing was edited and no regions were missing. An input such as an existing `bare_doc=True` spec whose template renders no managed blocks now refuses every refresh without force, whereas the previous code did not. The condition should skip this refusal when `not bodies` (or otherwise exempt bare docs).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/regions.py: none_here

chunk_findings.detail: The by-date fallback in `_fixes` sets `_Fix.holding = frozenset(range(first, len(tags)))` as the set of tags that contain a fixed security bug when the fix has no merged SHA. `tags` is established to be version-ordered, not date-ordered: an old maintenance tag like `1.5.9` can be dated after a newer major tag `2.0.0` and still sort at index 0. If a fixed security bug has `fixed_at` between the two dates and no merge info, `_by_date` returns the earlier index (`1.5.9`) because its date is after `fixed_at`, so the range includes the later index `2.0.0` even though `2.0.0` was released before the fix date and cannot contain it. Concretely, with `tags=[1.5.9 (2026-02-01), 2.0.0 (2026-01-01)]` and `fixed_at=2026-01-15`, the fix gets `holding={0,1}`. `_vulnerable` then sees `2.0.0` (index 1) as fixed and does not mark it vulnerable, so the generated SECURITY.md wrongly claims `2.0.0` already contains the fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_fixes

chunk_findings.detail: The new `target_of` still probes filesystem layout directly with `os.path.isfile(Path(repo) / rel)`, and `ddflow/services/export/refresh.py:_one` now relies on it. The rule requires filesystem layout to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`; the triage that "no filesystem port offers a stat" does not answer this, because the way to comply is to add/use the port rather than add a second direct call and defer ADP-fs. For example, with a SECURITY.md already present at `.github/SECURITY.md`, `target_of` calls the real OS `os.path.isfile`, so a fake filesystem adapter cannot intercept or replace the check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:target_of [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts that `[export.security] deprecated_lines = ["2.0"]` makes the current release line (`v2.0.0`, the newest tag) render as `"deprecated"` in the Supported Versions table. That contradicts the change’s own intent that the current release line is supported. With this behavior, an operator deprecating only the current line gets a SECURITY.md with no supported version, misleading users. If the implementation instead keeps the current line supported, this test is wrong and blocks the intended behavior. The change should either keep the current release line as `"supported"` regardless of `deprecated_lines`, or validation should reject deprecating the current line.

chunk_findings.detail: When a fixed security bug has a valid `fixed_at` and every tag’s `instant` is known, but no tag is at or after that instant (or `tags` is empty), `held` is empty and the new function returns `_Fix(frozenset(), by_date=True)`. The code this replaces returned `_Fix(placed=False)` for exactly this “no tag after the fix” case, so `_Fix.placed` was the signal that no release actually contains the fix. For example, with tags `v1.0.0` and `v1.1.0` both before a bug’s `fixed_at` and no merged SHA, `_by_date` now produces an empty holding set while leaving `placed` at its default `True`; downstream code that chooses the fixing version from the holding set then has zero tags to choose from (`min(empty)` / `next(iter(empty))`), or it treats an unreleased fix as released. The empty-`held` case should still preserve `_Fix(placed=False)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_by_date

chunk_findings.detail: `collect()` passes every security-tagged non-invalid bug to `_vulnerable()`, but `_vulnerable()` treats any bug without a `_Fix` as unfixed. A bug resolved `duplicate` (or `wontfix`, `notabug`) is not in `fixes` and `b.open` is false, so it is intentionally absent from the open/fixed known-issue lists, yet `_vulnerable()` still emits `vulnerable: <id>, not fixed yet` for the newest release. Concrete input: SEC-10 is tagged `security`, closed as duplicate of fixed bug SEC-0, and has no fix task. The SECURITY.md will permanently mark all current releases vulnerable to SEC-10, even though SEC-10 is a closed duplicate and SEC-0 is fixed. `_vulnerable()` should ignore non-open bugs that are not in `fixes`, matching the known-issues scope of open and fixed bugs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_vulnerable

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper queries the filesystem directly with `os.path.isfile(Path(repo) / rel)` instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, contrary to [r-adapters]. This is a new external dependency in `ddflow/services/export/ops.py`—e.g. every `target_of(repo, spec)` call performs ad-hoc filesystem-layout access that cannot be swapped or faked through the adapter layer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:target_of

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper’s docstring promises “a blank line before each” appended missing region, but it builds `block` with `"\n".join(render_region(...) for n in names)`, which inserts only a single newline between consecutive region blocks. Since `render_region` returns a region ending at the end marker without a trailing newline (a newline after `-->` would be outside the region), using `force` to append more than one missing region produces adjacent end/start markers with no blank line, e.g. `<!-- ...:supported:end -->\n<!-- ...:known:start -->`. The exported SECURITY.md therefore loses the blank-line separation present in the template and can render its supported/known-issue sections incorrectly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/regions.py: _appended

chunk_findings.detail: The template says "Dependency advisories and security-pass findings are not recorded there, so they are not covered here," and the matching help text in ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md describes Known Issues as only "bugs tagged `security` or `secbug`." This contradicts the change's own intent: dependency advisories are required to be shown in the Supported Versions table as "vulnerable: <id>, fixed in <ver>", and Known Issues must include "findings of the security pass." Given a dependency advisory or a security-pass finding, the exported SECURITY.md tells readers the item is not covered (or is omitted if the backend follows this text), so the required security disclosure is missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2:48-49

chunk_findings.detail: This new test file violates [r-adapters]: the helper `git()` calls `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], ...)` directly, and later tests also manipulate the filesystem with `Path`/`os` instead of using the project’s adapter ports. The rule explicitly lists `git`, `subprocess tools`, and `filesystem layout` as external dependencies that must go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, with tests using fakes rather than real subprocesses. Any environment without `git` on `PATH` makes every fixture in this file fail with `FileNotFoundError`, and the tests are not isolated behind a swappable fake as required.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_security.py:git

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation of `_is_security` checks `bool(wanted & set(b.tags)) or (item is not None and bool(wanted & set(item.tags)))`. However, `b.tags` and `item.tags` are expected to be collections of strings, but if either `b.tags` or `item.tags` is `None` or not an iterable of strings (for instance, if `Item.tags` can be `None` or another type based on the core model), `set(b.tags)` or `set(item.tags)` will raise a `TypeError` when `collect(q)` is executed. Given the core model fields for bugs and items, `tags` might be `None`, leading to a crash on export execution.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: The new `none_here = len(sp.missing) == len(bodies)` is also true when `bodies` is empty — i.e. a bare-document export with no managed regions, a case the function already supports via its `bare_doc` parameter. For an existing bare-document target, `sp.missing` is empty, so `len(sp.missing) == len(bodies)` is `0 == 0`; without `--force` this sets `refuse` (“... has no ddflow region ...”) and `W._finish` refuses the write even though nothing was edited and no regions were missing. An input such as an existing `bare_doc=True` spec whose template renders no managed blocks now refuses every refresh without force, whereas the previous code did not. The condition should skip this refusal when `not bodies` (or otherwise exempt bare docs).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/regions.py: none_here
